findings.text: Spec §5 requires the drain directive to name "the single output file `drain.replies.json` and its `plan_digest`", but `argsFor` hands `compose` the result of `st.promptArtifact(dir)`, and `promptArtifact` still joins `reviewFile`, so `drainDirective` tells the agent "Write exactly one file, .verdict/state/<pr>/review.json" while the launcher asserts `drain.replies.json`; an agent that obeys its directive writes review.json and every `drain --agent` run is refused `no-review-artifact` (observed in the drain-plan eval: the stub agent's recorded argv reads "Write exactly one file, .verdict/state/7/review.json"), so the drafting leg only succeeds when the agent ignores the instruction.

`assertDrainDirective` checks only loose fragments (drain.json, threads.json, findings.json, the digest, defer, post nothing, untrusted data) and never asserts the prompt names `drain.replies.json`, so a directive naming the wrong output file passes; the stub agents in `evals/cases/drain-plan.sh` and `drain-refusals.sh` also hardcode the reply path, so no Go test or eval can observe the artifact name the prompt carries.

Reusing `execute` also reuses `run`'s review-artifact hints: a drain launch that writes nothing is refused `no-review-artifact` with the hint "run the printed command yourself (--print) to see why no review.json appeared", and a pre-existing draft is refused `stale-review-artifact` with "delete the stale review.json (or let the agent overwrite it)" (observed live for drain --agent) — neither names drain.replies.json and drain accepts no --print, so the operator is pointed at the wrong file and a flag the verb rejects.

The published `$defs.skip` description enumerates the skip reasons as "resolved, answered, bot-reply, already-replied, not-review-comment, or deferred", but `CheckDrafts` appends `no-draft` entries into the same `skipped[]` list (observed: `{"thread_id":"PRRT_solo","reason":"no-draft"}`) and spec §4.2 requires it, so the schema documentation describing a machine-readable enum omits a value the shipped code emits.
findings.quote: "/$defs/skip": "One thread left open and why: resolved, answered, bot-reply, already-replied, not-review-comment, or deferred.",

findings.text: The verb declares its own `defaultMax = "20"` beside `draincore.DefaultMaxThreads = 20`, and nothing reads the core constant, so the documented default has two sources that can drift silently (the usage text and the schema descriptions hardcode 20 a third time).

`checkBody` exempts `defer` from the non-empty body rule, but the published `drain-replies.schema.json` marks `body` as required on every reply (`["thread_id","waiting_comment_id","disposition","body"]`), so a defer draft written without a `body` key passes `CheckDrafts` while failing the schema the skill ships, leaving two contracts for the same file inconsistent.

`validateFields` re-unmarshals the whole replies array on every entry, so a drafts file with n replies is decoded n times (quadratic work over up to 100 entries of 4000-character bodies) purely to find unknown keys; decoding once into `[]map[string]json.RawMessage` would keep the same site names at linear cost.

`next` keys only off `fl.agent != ""`, so `drain <repo> <pr> --agent <name>` on a feed with zero pending threads — a run that launched no agent and left `drafts` null — still answers `"next": "post the drafts with verdict drain acme/app 7 --post"` (observed), naming a command that cannot succeed with no drafts; the spec says `next` names the command the run did not do.

The launch request built for `--agent` omits `JSONMode`, unlike `internal/run/run.go:118`, so under `drain --json` the agent child is not given `NO_COLOR=1` by `childEnv` and its raw escape codes can reach the recorded `.run.out` and `run.json` output tail.

The new paragraph documents `drain.json` and the agent-written `drain.replies.json`, but the manual's bundle-namespace contract above still lists the core artifacts without either file and states "Agents write only `review.json` (plus `verification.json`/`patch.json`/`report.md`/`replies.json`/`noreview.md` where a mode file says so)" plus the rule that anything else a verb adds must live under `x-*`, so two shipped bundle files contradict the documented namespace.
